opening.text: Two teams pull on a rope. If one person lets go, the whole team feels it. If everyone holds on, the rope holds.
Sustaining our Church leaders is like holding the rope. Let’s talk about what it means to hold on.

mainMessage.text: To sustain is to support. We raise our hand, but we also pray, listen and act. When we do, our leaders are lifted, and so are we. And the whole Church grows strong in unity.

blocks.text: More than a raised hand.
In the Church, things are done by common consent. A vote is a real promise. The Lord said this is done with prayer and faith.
And all things shall be done by common consent in the church, by much prayer and faith, for all things you shall receive by faith. Amen.
No person is to be ordained to any office in this church, where there is a regularly organized branch of the same, without the vote of that church;
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Sustaining the Prophets” from the October 2014 general conference.
The obligation that we make when we raise our hands … is a most sacred one.
We mean it when we raise our hand.
Holding the rope.
Paul asked the Saints to know their leaders and to esteem them for their work. He said leaders watch over our souls.

Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you.

And we beseech you, brethren, to know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you; And to esteem them very highly in love for their work’s sake. And be at peace among yourselves.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Sustaining the Prophets” from the October 2014 general conference. He described what we promise.
We will stand behind him; we will pray for him; we will defend his good name.
It is a promise to stay with them.
Pray for them.
Paul asked us to pray for all in authority. The early Saints met often to fast and pray.

I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.
And the church did meet together oft, to fast and to pray, and to speak one with another concerning the welfare of their souls.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Sustaining the Prophets” from the October 2014 general conference.
Our sustaining of prophets is a personal commitment that we will do our utmost to uphold their prophetic priorities.
Prayer is one of the best ways to hold the rope.
Safety in counsel.
The Proverbs say there is safety in many counselors. In the Church, the Presidency is upheld by the confidence, faith and prayer of the members.
Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.

Of the Melchizedek Priesthood, three Presiding High Priests, chosen by the body, appointed and ordained to that office, and upheld by the confidence, faith, and prayer of the church, form a quorum of the Presidency of the Church.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Sustaining the Prophets” from the October 2014 general conference.
We will strive to carry out his instructions as the Lord shall direct.
We do our part when we act on what they teach.
Many hands, one body.
Paul said we are many members in one body. When one member suffers or is honored, all feel it.
For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office: So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.
And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Sustaining the Prophets” from the October 2014 general conference.
We sustain you, not only with uplifted hands but with all our hearts and consecrated efforts.
We help when we give our hearts too.
One eye, one faith.
Alma asked his people to have no contention and to be knit together in love. Paul said leaders are given for the perfecting of the Saints.

And he commanded them that there should be no contention one with another, but that they should look forward with one eye, having one faith and one baptism, having their hearts knit together in unity and in love one towards another.

For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ:
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Sustaining the Prophets” from the October 2014 general conference.
…as it comes through the voice of His servants the prophets.
Together we are strong.

story.title: Hands held up

blocks.text: Israel was in battle. Moses stood on a hill with his hands raised.

And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. But Moses’ hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
Moses grew tired. Aaron and Hur held up his arms. Leaders need that kind of help, and so do we.
